Arc Raiders is a interesting game with varied intensity, a solid atmosphere as well as great potential.

The Expedition system however is nothing but a time sink which ought to be revised.

I have tried to like this game, I really have but I can’t for longer than a few games at a time. I’ve never been fond of games like this and Arc raiders is my first. I got it because a buddy who doesn’t like these kinds of games like me agreed to try it with me, while he has since grown to like the game I just can’t. 

-It’s got good views, I am not one for graphics but this game is really nice visually. 
-It has very interesting weapons, I like the shields, I love the scrap like guns the most particularly the Rattler but it's just not a great choice sadly so I leave it behind a lot. 
-The loot is always interesting, some relics and most scrap. It is just a fun way to see what resources are available. 
-PvE is fun. It is a challenge and your costly and neater weapons thrive here.
PvP is just…..whoever shoots first wins.
-Other players while some are very nice others just aren’t what most would call good people. I’ve been killed for coming to someone’s rescue. Killed because I was standing there. Rushed for no reason while I was helping another person look for something they needed. Randomly shot and unlooted in one of my first games on buried city.
-The maps are great, wide and open and cramped at the same time. Spaceport is my favourite. I really liked taking an osprey to the breachedable bunker south of the South launch towers and sniping at Arc to help cover people during the Launch tower loot event.
-The idea that is Raiders versus the Arc is great in concept but with the threat of other Raiders drawing on you is a fantastic idea but other Raiders just don’t care that we’re all from Speranza and in theory on the same side working to support our subterranean community.     
-The quests are bland and if you play for a while before doing many of the quests you have already done what the quests have wanted you to do ten times over taking out the challenge and even the fun from quests.
-The sound is amazing in the game and the devs knew what they were doing by making similar audio cues between the environment and Arc. I always look up for a Rocketter when the elevator comes buzzing up even if I’m looking at the Rocketter already. 

I’ve liked seeing people argue it is just a game online but it isn’t just a game. It is a reflection of you.

Be kind, lend a hand and we’ll all make it to extract together. A simple idea but there's always a dozen that think your stuff is theirs by right of nothing. The game was okay but simply bad people have killed it’s barely okay fun.

[b]For [i]ARC Raiders[/i], Embark made the decision to train AI to use and recreate the voices of voice actors. This meant they would not need to ask the voice actors to come in to record new pings and voice lines for every new update. My understanding is that the voice actors were paid to have their voices used and recreated, but it is unclear whether they will be paid for every subsequent use or recreation of their voice. Either way, I feel this is a really scummy practise and it creates a worse product overall. The AI-generated voice acting in this game is bland, boring and lacks any character or emotion. [i]ARC Raiders[/i] may have an extremely pro-consumer business model, but I don't for a second believe that Embark could not now afford to get the voice actors back in to record over the AI-generated lines.[/b]

Once you get past the unethical and unforgivable use of AI-generated voice lines, [i]ARC Raiders[/i] is a phenomenal game that has some of the most unique PvE combat I have ever played. Most good PvE experiences thrive off of how fun it is to control your character; whether from a power fantasy, movement system or getting better loot. In ARC Raiders, the main thing that pulls me back in to the game is the interactions and combat with the PvE enemies. Seeing a wasp rebalance itself after you shoot off one of its thrusters, a leaper organically climb over surfaces to chase down a raider or a rocketeer flank an enemy to get the perfect angle for a rocket will never get old. The way these ARC enemies think, adapt and react to its surroundings is an overwhelmingly impressive feat unto itself. I haven't even mentioned the amazing world building, systems that allow for players to organically choose between a PvE, PvP or PvPvE experience and the amazing sound mix.

[i]ARC Raiders[/i] really is something special. As an original sceptic, I am so glad that I was proven wrong. Now Embark, all I need from you is to do the right thing and replace the AI-slop voice acting.
